newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Bahrain could attend Gulf Arab summit - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain could attend Gulf Arab summit - paper.

text.p: Bahrain might reconsider and attend December's Gulf Arab summit in Qatar if the problems prompting its boycott were eliminated, a Bahraini minister said in remarks published on Thursday.

"Cabinet Affairs and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said Bahrain would not refrain from attending the Doha summit if the reasons upon which Bahrain based its position were removed," said an article in Kuwait's al-Rai al-Aam newspaper based on an interview with Mutawae.
Bahrain's Foreign Minister Sheikh Mohammad bin Mubarak al-Khalifa said on Wednesday his country would not attend the summit in Qatar "because of unfriendly attitudes Qatar is taking against Bahrain."
Qatar has gone to the International Court of Justice over a small group of barren, but potentially valuable islands, sandbanks and reefs controlled by Bahrain but also claimed by Qatar.
The move has angered Bahrain which insists on a Gulf Arab solution.
"Bahrain still welcomes any Gulf move that would change the unfriendly positions of the Qatari leadership towards Bahrain," the paper said.
Qatar has said it would only withdraw the court case if mediation by Saudi Arabia, the region's dominant power, succeeded in resolving the dispute.

The Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) -- a political and economic alliance grouping Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and the United Arab Emirates -- is to hold its annual summit in Doha on December 7.

"Bahrain was an enthusiastic supporter for the establishment of the GCC and will not abandon it," the paper quoted Mutawae as saying. "(But) as long as these...circumstances exist, nothing would change in Bahrain's position on not attending the summit."
